records.location_name: Lassen Volcanic National Park; Sierra Nevada of Sierra-Nevada-Placer Counties Above 5000 ft Including Interstate 80; Sierra Nevada of El Dorado-Amador-Northern Alpine Counties Above 5000 ft Including Highway 50; Sierra Nevada of Calaveras-Tuolumne-Southern Alpine Counties Above 5000 ft
records.claim_text: NOAA alert 'Winter Storm Watch' for Lassen Volcanic National Park; Sierra Nevada of Sierra-Nevada-Placer Counties Above 5000 ft Including Interstate 80; Sierra Nevada of El Dorado-Amador-Northern Alpine Counties Above 5000 ft Including Highway 50; Sierra Nevada of Calaveras-Tuolumne-Southern Alpine Counties Above 5000 ft.

source_metadata.noaa_description:
* WHAT...Snow is expected for elevations above 6000 feet. Total snow
accumulations up to a foot, with up to 2 feet at the highest peaks.
Minor accumulations of around an 1 inch possible down to 5000 feet.
Winds could gust as high as 60 mph.

* WHERE...Northern Sierra above 6000 feet, including Highway 50,
Interstate 80, State Route 4, State Route 108, Southern Cascades
above 6000 feet, including Lassen National Park.

* WHEN...From Friday morning through Monday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult. The hazardous conditions
could impact the Friday evening and Monday morning commutes. Strong
winds could cause downed tree branches, localized power outages,
near whiteout conditions.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Snow levels 6500 to 7500 feet Friday, dropping
to 5500 to 6500 feet Saturday morning. Levels increase Sunday
morning to 6500 to 7500 feet before lowering again to 5500 to 6500
feet Monday. Heaviest snowfall expected Friday night into Saturday
morning. Light flurries to an inch possible down to 5000 feet with
higher accumulations remaining above 6000 feet. Lull in activity
Saturday afternoon and evening, followed by additional snow
Saturday night through Monday.
source_metadata.noaa_instruction:
Check the latest road conditions from Caltrans online at
quickmap.dot.ca.gov or dial 5 1 1.

records.claim_text: NOAA alert 'Wind Advisory' for South-Central Shasta County Including Redding Metro; Northern Sacramento Valley in Tehama County; Central Glenn County Including Interstate 5; Eastern Glenn County; Butte County Below 1000 ft.

source_metadata.noaa_description:
* WHAT...South winds 15 to 25 mph with gusts up to 45 mph expected.

* WHERE...Northern Sacramento Valley and portions of the central
Sacramento Valley.

* WHEN...From 4 AM to 7 PM PST Friday.

* IMPACTS...Gusty winds will blow around unsecured objects. Tree
limbs could be blown down and a few power outages may result.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Strongest winds expected Friday afternoon.
source_metadata.noaa_instruction:
Winds this strong can make driving difficult, especially for high
profile vehicles. Use extra caution.

records.location_name: Burke; Renville; Northwest Ward; Central and Southern Ward/Minot Area
records.claim_text: NOAA alert 'Special Weather Statement' for Burke; Renville; Northwest Ward; Central and Southern Ward/Minot Area.

source_metadata.noaa_description:
Patchy dense fog will reduce the visibility to one quarter mile
or less in parts of Ward, Burke, and Renville Counties through
mid-afternoon. Motorists should be prepared for rapidly changing
visibilities, and should use extra caution traveling. Use your
headlights and be extra cautious at intersections and railroad
crossings.

records.location_name: Surprise Valley California; Northern Washoe County
records.claim_text: NOAA alert 'High Wind Watch' for Surprise Valley California; Northern Washoe County.

source_metadata.noaa_description:
* CHANGES...None.

* WHAT...South to southwest winds 30 to 40 mph with gusts up to 65
mph.

* WHERE...In California, Surprise Valley California. In Nevada,
Northern Washoe County.

* WHEN...From Friday morning through Friday evening.

* IMPACTS...Damaging winds could blow down trees and power lines.
Widespread power outages are possible. Travel could be difficult,
especially for high profile vehicles.
source_metadata.noaa_instruction:
Now is the time to secure loose outdoor items such as patio
furniture, holiday decorations, and trash cans before winds increase
which could blow these items away. The best thing to do is prepare
ahead of time by making sure you have extra food and water on hand,
flashlights with spare batteries and/or candles in the event of a
power outage.
